items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S155

SPONSOR: HELMING
 
PURPOSE:

This legislation would create statewide process for determining which
officials may be granted peace officer status.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Criminal Procedure Law to designate various classes
of persons as peace officers. This includes, but is not limited to,
parole and warrant officers, probation officers, officials of the
Department of Corrections and Community Supervision, uniformed court
officers, constables, harbor masters, fire inspectors and marshalls,
those employed by a college, university, sheriff or police department as
members of the security force of a college or university, the welfare
inspector general, the workers' compensation fraud inspector general,
parks, recreation or forest rangers and special policemen.

Sections 2 through 32 amend coordinating sections of law to make
conforming changes.

Section 32 establishes an effective date of 180 days after it shall
become law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In past years, the Governor has vetoed bills that would grant peace
officer status to various officials. In his veto memos, he has recom-
mended that the Legislature create a comprehensive process for determin-
ing which categories of officials, on a statewide basis, should be
granted peace officer status. This legislation, drafted by the DCJS, is
a blanket wide bill designed to address the state's needs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.
